title: Flutter's Three Trees: UI Magic Explained

scenes.line1: How does Flutter update UI so fast?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how Flutter keeps your app's interface snappy, even when things change? Let's break down the secret.

scenes.label: Widget
scenes.sub: The widget tree defines the UI layout and structure.
scenes.say: First, the widget tree lays out what your app looks like. It’s just a blueprint for the interface.

scenes.label: Element
scenes.sub: The element tree manages widget instances and their state.
scenes.say: Next, the element tree keeps track of widget instances and their state. This is where changes actually happen.

scenes.label: Render
scenes.sub: The render tree handles layout and painting.
scenes.say: Finally, the render tree is in charge of drawing and laying out everything on screen.
When state changes, Flutter updates the element tree, rebuilds the widget tree, and repaints only the parts of the render tree that need it. That’s how it stays fast.

scenes.question: Does Flutter redraw the whole UI?
scenes.right: No, only affected parts of the render tree are updated. The rest stays untouched for performance.
scenes.say: A common mistake is thinking Flutter redraws everything. Actually, it only updates what’s changed, keeping things efficient.
